source: https://aiyprojects.withgoogle.com/vision/ (Google AIY Vision Kit V1.2, $90 at launch per https://magazine.raspberrypi.com/articles/aiy-projects-2-pi-zero-wh): Pi Zero WH, Pi Camera v2 with long and short flex cables, Vision Bonnet, push button and harness, a privacy LED in a bezel next to the lens, microSD, 2 standoffs, cardboard case. Gives controller, storage, camera, camera-cable, carrier-board, button, camera-light, fastener. https://aiyprojects.withgoogle.com/voice/ and https://aiyprojects.readthedocs.io/en/latest/voice.html (Google AIY Voice Kit, $49 for V2): Pi Zero WH, Voice HAT V1 with 2 ICS-43432 I2S mics and a MAX98357A amp, button on GPIO23 (V2 Voice Bonnet: 2 mics, codec, LED driver), speaker, push button with LED, microSD, 2 standoffs, a 2.1 A micro-USB supply bought separately. Gives microphone x2, amplifier, speaker, button, wake-light, power-supply. https://us.ipevo.com/pages/v4k-specs (IPEVO V4K USB document camera, $115 at https://us.ipevo.com/products/v4k-store): 8 MP head on a multi-jointed arm over a base, 342 x 255 mm capture area, 581 g. Gives arm, ballast and the base and head shells. https://github.com/rhasspy/wyoming-satellite/blob/master/docs/tutorial_2mic.md runs a Pi Zero 2 W with a 2-mic HAT as a voice satellite, so the Zero 2 W is enough for cloud voice. None of these has a hardware mic mute: mic-mute-switch, mute-light and the USB-C inlet come from Ponder's brief (hardware-notes.md); the Pi Zero 2 W only has micro-USB, so a USB-C supply needs an inlet.

roles.spec: Raspberry Pi Zero-class board with on-board Wi-Fi and a 40-pin header (AIY kits: Pi Zero WH; now Pi Zero 2 W)
microSD card with Raspberry Pi OS
Raspberry Pi camera module that sees a whole Letter or A4 page from about 220-250 mm (about 70 deg diagonal or wider) and focuses near 25 cm
flex cable for the Zero's 22-pin camera connector
HAT or bonnet on the Pi header that carries the audio, button and light wiring (AIY Voice HAT or Vision Bonnet; a protoboard bonnet when built from breakouts)
I2S MEMS microphone
I2S class-D mono amp, MAX98357A class
about 40 mm, 4 ohm, 3 W
5 V USB wall supply, 2.5 A or more
USB-C 5 V inlet on the case
one large momentary push-to-talk button
status light the child can see (AIY: LED in the button; brief: light strip on the base)
LED next to the lens, on while the camera is in use (AIY Vision privacy LED)
switch that physically cuts the microphones
light that shows the microphones are cut
current-limit resistors for the discrete LEDs
wires between base and head, run through the arm
arm that holds the head about 220 mm above the desk and about 120 mm forward of the base
steel or zinc weight in the base so the unit doesn't tip with the head over the page
printed base shell, top: speaker grille, button hole, arm mount
printed base plate that holds the ballast
printed head shell, upper: mic ports
printed head shell, lower: camera window
threaded inserts or standoffs for the board and the shells
machine screws that close the shells and hold the Pi

batchUsd.basis: 20 units bought in the US, prices read 2026-10-13, 10-99 tier where listed. Electronics $124-141 a unit: Pi Zero 2 W with header $19.80 (Adafruit 6008, out of stock) to $20.75 (PiShop); Raspberry Pi 32 GB card $13.69 (Adafruit 6010, no longer stocked) to $24.95 (SparkFun, out of stock); Camera Module 3 Wide $38.50 (Adafruit, PiShop); Zero camera cable $2.70; 2 SPH0645 mics at $6.26; MAX98357A $5.36; 40 mm 4 ohm speaker $4.46 (Adafruit 3968, out of stock) to $5.73 (PUI AS04004PR-R, Master Electronics, MOQ 20); 15 W USB-C supply $7.87; USB-C breakout $2.66; Perma Proto bonnet $4.05 (plus $3.56 for a base protoboard at the high end); NeoPixel stick $5.36; 16 mm button $1.35; DPDT toggle $1.13; ribbon harness $3.56; LEDs, resistors and diodes under $1. Mechanics about $44 a unit: 12 in gooseneck $24.32, 2 couplings at $1.76, nipples and nuts under $0.50 (Grand Brass); 2 steel discs at $6.32 (Wagner, 25+); M3 inserts, M3 and M2.5 screws about $2.40; feet $0.86. Printed shells $42-53 a unit for 150-175 cm3 of PA12 MJF: JLC3DP lists MJF-PA12 at $0.275/g (Aug 2025), about $0.28/cm3; the pipeline's Craftcloud rate is $0.30/cm3. Parts come to about $4,190-4,750; shipping from 5-6 shops adds $60-250, an allowance because the shops don't publish rates. Cross-checks: AIY Voice Kit V2 ($49) plus Vision Kit V1.2 ($90) was $139 of electronics in cardboard; an IPEVO V4K document camera (arm, base, 8 MP head, no audio or compute) is $115.
